tweets: Badrinath Temple, ochre-walled beneath Nīlkaṇṭha peak, marks one corner of the Char Dhām — Badrinath, Dwārkā, Puri, Rāmeśvaram, the four abodes spanning India's compass. Each winter its doors seal under snow, said to guard an untended lamp till spring.

Adi Śaṅkarācārya is credited with binding these four sites into one circuit in the 8th century CE, each tied to a Veda and a cardinal direction — epics made geography. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history.
